clue.text: "No Smoking" notice in the Park?

parts.note: grass is slang for cannabis, so a park sign telling people to stay off the lawn can be read as a ban on smoking dope

explanation.surface: A sign forbidding cigarettes put up in a public park.
explanation.walkthrough: The familiar park sign protecting the lawn doubles as an anti-drugs notice because grass is slang for marijuana.
explanation.definitionFit: The sign telling walkers not to tread on the lawn is a common park notice, punningly read here as a drugs ban.

clue.text: Put together a leap at the ballet

definitions.meaning: to put together is to gather or construct, a verb sense
in ballet the term names a jump in which the feet come together in the air

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means gather or build, and the same word is also a French ballet term for a jump with feet joined.

clue.text: Try speaking here

indicators.note: speaking signals that the next word is said out loud and a word of the same sound is entered

parts.note: taken as the word said aloud

explanation.surface: An invitation to have a go at saying something on this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge who tries a case is said to hear it, a legal synonym.

clue.text: Product of a Lancing assembly?

indicators.note: an assembly is a putting together, so the letters of the two words are rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: Asks what comes out of a gathering at a Sussex school.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancing College is a Church of England boarding school in Sussex, so its assembly would turn out churchgoers of that communion; the letters of A LANCING rearrange to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil formed by a Church of England school's assembly would be a member of that church.

clue.text: One of the best of Paris toffs

indicators.note: of says the answer is made of letters taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A Parisian socialite counted among the finest of that city's upper-class set.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans the end of Paris and the start of toffs.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristocracy literally means rule by the best, so a member of the nobility is one of the best people.

clue.text: Around the M25?

parts.note: the M25 is the orbital motorway encircling London, so it is a road going round, and a word meaning round fits it

explanation.surface: A question about travelling round London's ring motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M25 is the motorway that runs in a ring around London.
explanation.definitionFit: Something going round in a ring describes the orbital motorway and also means around.

clue.text: She was a Queen of Man (island)

parts.note: a man is referred to as he
Cuba is a Caribbean island

explanation.surface: A woman who reigned over the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen of Man (island)' suggests the Isle of Man, but Man and island are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend she was the wife of Priam and queen of Troy.

clue.text: A fast and friendly horse

parts.note: fast can mean firmly fixed and friendly suggests a mate, so the clue describes a horse sharing quarters with another as its pal

explanation.surface: A speedy racehorse with a sociable temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: Fast seems to mean quick, but it hints at steady and settled, and a horse kept in the same yard as another is its fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse trained in the same yard as another is its fellow, and the phrase extends to any close associate.

clue.text: A Nepalese, say, is earnest about monarch

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters are mixed up into a new order

parts.note: ER is the royal cipher of Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A man from Nepal shows seriousness concerning a king or queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a container signal, but here it means jumbled, and the monarch is the royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Nepal comes from the East, so is an example of an Oriental person.

clue.text: It's useless putting catmint in it

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
nep is an old name for the plant catmint

explanation.surface: Feeding a cat some catnip is said to be pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Useless and clumsy are both senses of incompetent or lacking skill.

clue.text: More than one sound in cavity wall

indicators.note: sound tells us the words before it are said aloud and the entry is a word that sounds the same

parts.note: more than one describes a grammatical number for several things

explanation.surface: Several noises can be heard inside a hollow brick wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavity wall' is a building term, but here it is the membrane lining the chest cavity; the adjective describes that lining.
explanation.definitionFit: The pleura is the membrane lining the chest cavity, and the adjective describes things belonging to that lining.

clue.text: Without hesitation diced cucumbers deteriorate

indicators.note: diced means chopped up, so the remaining letters are cut up and rearranged
without says some letters are taken away from the word that follows

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating in speech

explanation.surface: Chopped cucumbers go off quickly if left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' removes ER from CUCUMBERS to leave CUCUMBS, which 'diced' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To give way or yield to illness or decline is to fall away, a loose synonym for worsening.

clue.text: One of these watch chains was free on board

definitions.text: One of these watch chains was free on board

parts.words: One of these watch chains was free on board
parts.note: the singular word is also the shipping abbreviation for free on board, so one such chain is that abbreviation

explanation.surface: A pocket-watch chain is said to have travelled without charge on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: In shipping, goods sold free on board have their loading paid by the seller; the initials of that phrase spell one of these chains.
explanation.definitionFit: Short chains attaching pocket watches to waistcoats share their name with the shipping abbreviation.

clue.text: Dolphin's friend?

parts.note: dolphins swim in groups called schools, so a fellow member of the group is a classmate of sorts

explanation.surface: Asks who a dolphin's companion might be.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow pupil is a friend from class, and dolphins travel in pods also called schools.

clue.text: The crime of corrupt senator

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Names the offence committed by a dishonest politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country is the gravest crime against the state.

clue.text: Fixer who betrayed King Edward twice

parts.note: to sell someone out is to betray them

indicators.note: twice asks for the following piece to appear two times in a row

parts.note: ER is Edwardus Rex, the cipher of a King Edward

explanation.surface: A man who sorted things out turned traitor against a monarch twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who joins metal with molten alloy fixes things together.

clue.text: Twister whirling to and fro leaving France

indicators.note: whirling means spinning round, so the remaining letters are mixed up
leaving says a letter departs from the phrase before any rearranging

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: A storm spins back and forth before moving away from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving France' takes F out of TO AND FRO, leaving TOANDRO for 'whirling' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is an informal name for a violent rotating windstorm.

clue.text: The Dogs of War?

parts.note: the part-time soldiers of the Territorial Army were nicknamed after a breed group of dog

explanation.surface: Echoes the Shakespeare phrase about the hounds of battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve force; its soldiers were nicknamed Terriers, a breed name.
explanation.definitionFit: Small hunting dogs give their name to British reserve soldiers, so they are literally dogs of war.

clue.text: Flexible expert adopts different name

indicators.note: adopts means takes in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an able person is skilled or expert

indicators.note: different means altered, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: An adaptable specialist takes on a new name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopts' seems to mean taking on a new name in the surface, but it signals putting the rearranged letters inside the word for expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone willing and easily persuaded is pliant, so flexible fits as a synonym.

clue.text: They provide increases for the upwardly mobile

definitions.text: They provide increases for the upwardly mobile

parts.words: They provide increases for the upwardly mobile
parts.note: the social-climbing sense of upwardly mobile is misleading: the clue means people literally moving up, carried on moving stairs

explanation.surface: Something that gives social climbers pay rises.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving staircases lift people from one floor to the next, so they literally carry them upward.

clue.text: It's clean'd out with a snuffer

definitions.text: It's clean'd out with a snuffer

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something is cleared away by a device for dousing flames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' also works in the &lit sense: a snuffer puts this out.
explanation.definitionFit: A wax light with a wick is extinguished with a snuffer.

clue.text: Donald's master cards

definitions.meaning: in card games the cards of the chosen suit beat all others

explanation.definitionFit: The surname of businessman Donald with a possessive matches the plural word for the winning card suit.

clue.text: Make them pay for smuggling drug

indicators.note: smuggling means carrying something secretly, so the answer is concealed within the words

explanation.surface: Smugglers of narcotics should be made to suffer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis is obtained from the plant, so its name serves for the drug.

clue.text: Poem composed around Elizabeth's inauguration

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are arranged anew
an inauguration is a beginning, so only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Verse written to mark the start of a queen's reign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal, but it is fodder; 'inauguration' takes E from Elizabeth's.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a short French verse form with a refrain, a kind of poem.

clue.text: To install firmly fix in a ring

indicators.note: to fix can mean to rig or arrange, so the letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Setting something solidly by securing it in a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix a habit or dye deeply into something is to embed or establish it firmly.

clue.text: Is it blown when the foreman blabs?

definitions.text: Is it blown when the foreman blabs?

parts.words: Is it blown when the foreman blabs?
parts.note: a British idiom says a secret is blown when someone lets it slip, and a works foreman is called by a slang name built on the same short word

explanation.surface: Asks whether something is ruined when the boss talks too much.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a foreman is a gaffer, and blowing the secret means giving the game away; the answer is the thing blown in that idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The word appears in the idiom for letting out a secret and also starts the slang word for a boss.

clue.text: Comfort for the free slave

indicators.note: free means released, so the letters are loosed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Liberating a slave brings relief.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothing ointment, and figuratively anything that soothes, offers comfort.

clue.text: A case a minister could be without

definitions.meaning: a flat carrying case for papers or drawings
a minister without ... holds cabinet rank but has no department

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a document case and the department a government minister holds.
